facts.text: The period studied so far was from the year 1961 to 2000; the speed of change in the twentieth and twenty-first centuries has been tremendous.
facts.quote: So far, we have studied the period from the year 1961 to 2000. The speed of change in the twentieth and the twenty-first centuries has been tremendous.

facts.text: Modernisation has posed some challenges before all religions: Hinduism, Islam, Christianity, Sikhism, Jainism, Buddhism, Zoroastrianism and Judaism.
facts.quote: Now, modernisation has posed some challenges before all religions, be it Hinduism, Islam, Christianity, Sikhism, Jainism, Buddhism, Zoroastrianism or Judaism.

facts.text: Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar brought about a sea change in our traditional mindset through the medium of the Indian Constitution.
facts.quote: Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar brought about a sea change in our traditional mindset. He brought it about through the medium of the Indian Constitution.

facts.text: According to the Constitution, all Indians are equal before the law and cannot be discriminated against on the basis of religion, race, caste, gender or place of birth.
facts.quote: According to our Constitution, all Indians are equal before the law, and they cannot be discriminated against on the basis of religion, race, caste, gender or place of birth.

facts.text: All citizens have freedom of speech and expression, to assemble peacefully without arms, to form associations, to move, live and settle anywhere in India and to practise any occupation.
facts.quote: All citizens have the right to freedom of speech and expression, freedom to assemble peacefully without arms, freedom to form associations, freedom to move, to live and settle down anywhere on Indian territory and to practice any occupation.

facts.text: Indian citizens living anywhere in India enjoy the right to nurture their language, script and culture.
facts.quote: Indian citizens living anywhere in India enjoy the right to nurture their language, script and culture.

facts.text: These provisions shook the foundations of the caste system and helped make vocations running in the family obsolete.
facts.quote: These provisions in the Constitution shook the foundations of the caste system. It helped to make the practice of vocations running in the family obsolete.

facts.text: Now anyone can go into a restaurant irrespective of religion, race, caste or gender; boards outside restaurants welcome all.
facts.quote: Now, anyone can go into a restaurant irrespective of his religion, race, caste or gender. In fact, we see boards outside the restaurants welcoming all.

facts.text: After independence citizens got the right to express opinions against the government, through newspapers, speeches or other media.
facts.quote: Another very significant change during the post-independence period is the right to express opinions against the government. ... Now Indian citizens can register their protest against the policies of the government through newspapers, speeches or other media.

facts.text: During the British era, trains had four kinds of compartments: first, second, inter and third class; third class passengers got nominal facilities.
facts.quote: During the British era, there were four kinds of compartments in the railway train - the first, second, inter and third class. Nominal facilities for the passengers travelling by third class ...

facts.text: In the 1978 Railway Budget, Madhu Dandawate put an end to the third class.
facts.quote: In the 1978 Railway Budget, Madhu Dandawate put an end to this third class.

facts.text: Two trains with no class divisions were started: 'Sinhagad Express' on the Pune-Mumbai route and 'Gitanjali Express' on the Mumbai-Kolkata route.
facts.quote: Later two trains were started which had no class divisions, namely, 'Sinhagad Express' on the Pune-Mumbai route and 'Gitanjali Express' on the Mumbai-Kolkata route.

facts.text: India was known all over the world as the country of joint families; the wave of globalisation has given an impetus to nuclear families.
facts.quote: India was known all over the world as the country of joint families. However, the wave of globalisation has now given an impetus to the system of nuclear families.

facts.text: The objective to establish the welfare state is in the Constitution itself; India is the first country in the world to do so.
facts.quote: The objective to establish the welfare state has been incorporated in the Constitution itself. India is the first country in the world to do so.

facts.text: Social welfare programmes aim to make full-time employment, health care, education and development available to all Indian citizens.
facts.quote: The social welfare programmes aim to make opportunities for full-time employment, health care, education and development available to all Indian citizens.

facts.text: On 14 June 1964 the government of India constituted the Ministry of Social Welfare.
facts.quote: That is why, on 14th June 1964, the government of India constituted the Ministry of Social Welfare.

facts.text: Under the Ministry of Social Welfare, programmes run for nutrition and child-development, social security and social protection, and women's welfare and development.
facts.quote: Under this ministry various programmes are implemented for nutrition and child-development, social security and social protection, women's welfare and development.

facts.text: According to the 1971 Census, 22% people in India belonged to scheduled castes and tribes.
facts.quote: According to the 1971 Census, 22% people in India belonged to scheduled castes and tribes.

facts.text: Laws gave scheduled castes and tribes educational scholarships and representation in Parliament and State Assemblies; some seats are reserved for them in Government services.
facts.quote: Laws were enacted so that they got educational scholarships, and representation in Parliament as well State Assemblies. Some seats are also reserved for them in Government services.

facts.text: The Constitution says the primary duty of the government is to raise the people's standard of living, ensure proper nutrition and improve public health.
facts.quote: The Constitution of India states that the primary duty of the government is to raise the people's standard of living, to ensure proper nutrition and to improve public health.

facts.text: An objective of the Sixth Five Year plan was to make primary health services and medical care available to rural people, the tribals and the poor.
facts.quote: To make primary health services as well as medical care available to rural people, the tribals and the poor was an objective of the Sixth Five Year plan.

facts.text: Unani, Homoeopathy, Ayurveda and Naturopathy were given recognition in addition to Allopathy.
facts.quote: Efforts were made towards helping people maintain good health by giving recognition to Unani, Homoeopathy, Ayurveda and Naturopathy in addition to Allopathy.

facts.text: In 1962 the first successful open heart surgery was performed under Dr N. Gopinath at Christian Medical College Hospital, Vellore, Tamil Nadu.
facts.quote: In 1962, the first successful open heart surgery was performed under the leadership of Dr N. Gopinath at Christian Medical College Hospital at Vellore in Tamil Nadu.

facts.text: Jaipur Foot: before 1968 a person who lost a leg suffered for life; Dr Pramod Sethi designed and made artificial limbs, noses and ears with the help of the skilled craftsman Ramchandra Sharma.
facts.quote: Similarly, the invention of the 'Jaipur Foot' has transformed the lives of the disabled in India. Before 1968, if a person lost a leg in an accident, he had to suffer for the rest of his life. In order to remedy the situation, Dr Pramod Sethi designed and manufactured artificial limbs, noses and ears, with the help of the skilled craftsman Ramchandra Sharma.

facts.text: With Jaipur foot limbs people can walk bare-foot on rough surfaces, run, cycle, climb trees and mountains, bend at the knees and sit cross-legged; no footwear is needed.
facts.quote: ... have made it easy for the differently abled to walk bare-foot on rough surfaces, run, go cycling, work in the fields, climb trees, and even climb mountains, etc. They save on the expenses on shoes ... They can bend their legs at the knees and sit cross-legged.

facts.text: In 1971 a kidney transplant was successfully performed at the Christian Medical College hospital at Vellore; Dr Johny and Dr Mohan Rao transplanted a kidney donated by a living person.
facts.quote: But in 1971, it was successfully performed at the Christian Medical College hospital at Vellore in Tamil Nadu. Dr Johny and Dr Mohan Rao transplanted the kidney donated by a living person into the patient's body.

facts.text: Test-tube baby technology has been available since 1978; under Dr Subhash Mukhopadhyaya the experiment succeeded at Kolkata, the first successful attempt at artificial conception, and a girl named Durga was born.
facts.quote: The support of 'test-tube baby' technology has been available to childless couples since 1978. It was under the supervision of Dr Subhash Mukhopadhyaya that the experiment of the test-tube baby was successfully carried out at Kolkata. This was the first successful attempt at artificial conception. A girl named Durga was born.

facts.text: Before 1978, every year six Indian infants out of every 10 born faced fatal health problems in their first year.
facts.quote: Before 1978, every year, six Indian infants out of every 10 who were born faced fatal health problems in the very first year of their birth.

facts.text: The immunisation programme was taken up to overcome polio, measles, tetanus, TB, diphtheria and whooping cough.
facts.quote: The immunisation programme was taken up to overcome the threat of polio, measles, tetanus, TB, diphtheria, and whooping cough.

facts.text: The 'pulse polio' immunisation programme started in 1995 has controlled polio.
facts.quote: The 'pulse polio' immunisation programme started in 1995 has controlled polio.

facts.text: Urbanisation is the concentration of population in a city or urban area; increasing population is one major reason for it.
facts.quote: Urbanisation is a process of the concentration of population in a city or urban area. Increasing population is one major reason for urbanisation.

facts.text: After independence urban population grew also due to reduction in the mortality rate, industrialisation, lack of livelihood in rural areas, jobs in cities and migration.
facts.quote: In the context of post-independence India, the increase in urban population is also due to factors such as reduction in the mortality rate, industrialisation, unavailability of means of livelihood in rural areas, job opportunities in cities and the resulting migration.

facts.text: To reduce the strain on cities, jobs must be made available in villages, development balanced, the expansion of metros controlled and facilities given to urban and rural areas.
facts.quote: To reduce the strain on cities, it is necessary to make jobs available in villages, achieve a balance in economic development, control the expansion of metros and provide necessary services and facilities in both the urban as well as rural areas.

facts.text: A village is a permanent settlement of farmers near the land they themselves tilled; villages came into existence when farming began.
facts.quote: A village is a permanent settlement of farmers near the land they themselves tilled, either individually or collectively. Villages came into existence when farming began.

facts.text: A dense cluster of houses surrounded by farmland is a unique feature of the Indian village; a settlement smaller than a village is called a hamlet.
facts.quote: A dense cluster of houses surrounded by farmland is a unique feature of the Indian village. A settlement smaller than even a village is called a hamlet.

facts.text: Under the collective development scheme, rural development work was done through Gram Panchayats; Gram Panchayats, Panchayat Samitis and Zilla Parishads got more authority.
facts.quote: The government undertook this work through the medium of Gram Panchayats which included the people from all castes and tribes. To achieve this, the Gram Panchayats, Panchayat Samitis and Zilla Parishads were empowered with more authority.

facts.text: Earlier every village was economically self-sufficient, and farm produce was distributed among artisans as payment for their work.
facts.quote: Earlier, every village was economically self-sufficient. A majority of the villagers were dependent on farming. Farm produce used to be distributed among artisans as payment for their work.

facts.text: In 1961, 82% of India's population resided in villages; in 1971 the percentage was 80.01%.
facts.quote: In 1961, 82% of India's population resided in villages. In 1971, the percentage was 80.01%.

facts.text: Three major challenges of rural development: economic development, facilities to meet social needs, and a change of attitude in matters of society, culture and ways of thinking.
facts.quote: There are three major challenges with reference to rural development, namely, bringing about economic development, developing facilities to meet social needs and finally bringing about a change of attitude in matters concerning society, culture and ways of thinking.

facts.text: The collective development scheme had an important place in the first four five year plans; in Maharashtra, Zilla Parishads were established in 1962.
facts.quote: The collective development scheme had an important place in all the first four five year plans of the government of India. The State of Maharashtra registered remarkable achievements under this scheme. For example, 'Zilla Parishads' were established in 1962.

facts.text: Maharashtra launched a nutritious diet scheme in 1970-1971 and the 'Rural Water Supply Scheme' for wells and piped water; by 1971, 1677 small dams had been built.
facts.quote: Nutritious diet scheme was launched in 1970-1971. The State also started 'Rural Water Supply Scheme' for sinking wells and providing piped water. By 1971, 1677 small dams had also been built.

facts.text: Electricity is needed in villages for pumps, to preserve milk, eggs, fruits and vegetables, to run fertiliser projects, and for fans, TV and study lights.
facts.quote: Automatic pumps are needed to water the fields. Electricity is needed to preserve perishable food items such as milk, eggs, fruits and vegetables, to run fertiliser projects and for fans and TV and for lights for studying at night.

facts.text: During the first five year plan electricity reached three thousand villages; by 1973 it reached 1,38,646 villages.
facts.quote: During the first five year plan, electricity had been provided to three thousand villages in India. By 1973, it reached 1,38,646 villages.

facts.text: From 1966 it was decided to supply more electricity for pumps and borewells.
facts.quote: From 1966, it was decided to supply more electricity for pumps and borewells.

facts.text: The 'Rural Electrification Corporation' was established in 1969.
facts.quote: 'Rural Electrification Corporation' was established in 1969.

facts.text: Rural Electrification Co-operative Societies came into being in Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat, Karnataka, Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh.
facts.quote: 'Rural Electrification Co-operative Societies came into being in the States of Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat, Karnataka, Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh.

facts.text: A 'Village Industries Planning Committee' was formed for rural industry; by 1972, 1,06,000 persons got employment under this scheme.
facts.quote: A 'Village Industries Planning Committee' was formed to help the development of industry in rural areas. By 1972, 1,06,000 persons got employment under this scheme.

facts.text: Maharashtra started residential high schools called 'Vidya Niketan' in Satara, Aurangabad, Nasik and Chikhaldara for meritorious village students living in unfavourable conditions.
facts.quote: The government of Maharashtra has also started residential highschools known as 'Vidya Niketan' in Satara, Aurangabad, Nasik and Chikhaldara. Their purpose is to provide the best quality education to intelligent and meritorious village students living in unfavourable conditions.

facts.text: As per the Kothari Commission, Agriculture Universities were started at Rahuri, Akola, Parbhani and Dapoli in Maharashtra.
facts.quote: As per the recommendations of the Kothari Commission, Agriculture Universities were also started at Rahuri, Akola, Parbhani and Dapoli in Maharashtra.

facts.text: In 1972 UNESCO awarded its international prize for the spread of literacy to Maharashtra.
facts.quote: In recognition of the work done in the field of education, UNESCO awarded its international prize for the spread of literacy to Maharashtra in 1972.

facts.text: Before globalisation the rural community was small and homogeneous, with a larger proportion of family vocations and joint families; the urban community was large and heterogeneous, with fewer family vocations and a trend towards nuclear families.
facts.quote: Rural Community ... Small in size, homogeneous in terms of language, culture and tradition. ... Larger proportion of vocations running in the family. ... Joint family system. Urban Community ... Large in size, heterogeneous ... Less proportion of vocations running in the family. ... Trend towards - nuclear families.
